chunks: And whatever is in it from Umar ibn Abi Shu'bah, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Jafar ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Umar ibn Abi Shu'bah Al-Halabi.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him
key_terms.عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي شُعْبَةَ: Umar ibn Abi Shu'bah, a prominent narrator
key_terms.مَاجِيلَوَيْهَ: Majilawayh, a specific narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: Who is the chain of narrators for the hadiths from Umar ibn Abi Shu'bah in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous verification of the *isnad* for Umar ibn Abi Shu'ah Al-Halabi, a key narrator in the Kufan school. By tracing the chain through prominent figures like Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Khattab, al-Saduq underscores the reliability of these reports in the absence of the Imam, reflecting the Shia emphasis on rigorous biographical evaluation (*ilm al-rijal*) to preserve authentic jurisprudence.
